item.title: Louis Tomlinson Takes a Sunny New Direction
item.description: On his third solo album, the 1970s-inspired How Did I Get Here?, Louis Tomlinson executes a clear creative vision, but relies heavily on his boy band roots.

item.title: A Conversation with Guided By Voices’ Robert Pollard
item.description: The Guided By Voices machine is as well-oiled as they come, but Robert Pollard attributes quality and consistency to chemistry.

item.title: Justin Townes Earle’s Unrealized Future
item.description: Rolling Stone editor Jonathan Bernstein's biography of Justin Townes Earle, What Do You Do When You’re Lonesome, is rooted in the quiet devastation of Saint of Lost Causes.

item.title: Amy Grant’s “The 6th of January” Tells What’s Going On
item.description: Amy Grant's "The 6th of January" burns the way the Ramones' "Bonzo Goes to Bitburg" burned in denouncing Ronald Reagan's visit to a Nazi cemetery.

item.title: Sotto Voce’s Lo-Fi Pop Is Filled with Melodic Twists
item.description: Ryan Gabos' lo-fi bedroom pop project, Sotto Voce, scales new heights with The Sound of Trying.

item.title: ‘Playmakers’ Explores the Chutzpah That Made Kids’ Toys
item.description: Playmakers illustrates that many toys of American childhood came into being because their Jewish creators were shut out of the American workplace.

item.title: Dance Moms’ Ferocious Appetite
item.description: In the aftermath of the 2008 stock market crash, Dance Moms helped feed America's ferocious appetite for cruelty.

item.title: Craig Taborn Is at the Apex of Contemporary Jazz
item.description: In 2026, Craig Taborn and other improvisers of his generation are at the peak of their creativity. This music has rarely been more elevated, refined, and exciting.

item.title: M(h)aol’s ‘Something Soft’ Is a Post-#MeToo Gut-Punch
item.description: M(h)aol's Something Soft is a powerful feminist punk album. It highlights the stakes of inhabiting the female body in a world where safety is conditional and fleeting.

item.title: Kula Shaker Rally the Poets of Light on ‘Wormslayer’
item.description: Kula Shaker's Wormslayer is for the seeker, the adventurer, and the soul who longs for liberty—all while soundtracking their journey to an epic musical mirror.
